tiers.none: Nothing is claimed. The agent may work, but ORCA says nothing verified about what its policy covers.
tiers.A: Connects and fails closed: for each route, a passing installed receipt for the pinned agent, version and host shows the agent connects and that the uncovered routes listed are refused or asked about.
tiers.B: Approvals validated: for each route, a passing installed receipt for the pinned agent, version and host runs every case the route can run against the real agent.
tiers.C: Execution guard certified: for each route, a passing connected receipt for the pinned agent, version and host from a connected path that proves the route (a live agent, its adapter and ORCA together) runs every case that path can run, and that path excludes no lifecycle or bypass case.

receipts.note: A receipt is a JSON file committed under tools/guard-qualification/receipts/. It names kind (installed or connected), agent, agentVersion, adapterVersion, host, route, build (the 40-hex ORCA commit it ran), checks.connects, checks.uncoveredRoutesRefused and per-case results, with no case listed twice. It must match the row's pin (agentVersion, adapterVersion, host, build). Tiers are cumulative. Beside it is its Sigstore bundle (<receipt>.sigstore.json): a receipt counts only when its GitHub artifact attestation verifies, signed by .github/workflows/guard-receipts.yml on a GitHub-hosted runner, from main or a release line, at the receipt's build (tools/guard-qualification/attestation.js). Tiers A and B can be promoted on such receipts; tier C stays refused until #1026's independent observer exists. Synthetic receipts never count. A file path or a named residual risk is not proof.
